+=== Pure-Capability Register Convention
+
+Since the RVY capability registers extend the integer register file, the same conventions and names are used.
+The only difference is that they are `YLEN` bits wide and must be aligned to `YLEN` bits as well.
+Register usage follows the underlying ILP32*/LP64* ABIs with the only difference that `x5` is used for on-stack arguments (see <<pure-cap-on-stack-args>>).
+
+IMPORTANT: Capability register usage in the ILP32* and LP64* ABIs is not specified yet, only IL32PC64* and L64PC128* ABIs have a well-defined calling convention for capability registers.
+
+

+[[pure-cap-cc]]
+=== RVY Pure-Capability Calling Conventions
+
+IMPORTANT: RVY Pure-Capability ABIs are experimental.
+
+These calling conventions are used when the base ISA is RVY and a pure-capability ABI is in use.
+In these ABIs, all pointers (including the stack pointer, frame pointer, and return address) are represented as capabilities (using the extended GPRs).
+
+The register names and usage remain the same as the <<integer-cc,integer calling convention>>, but the registers `x0`-`x31` (and their ABI aliases) now refer to the `YLEN`-wide extended GPRs.
+Any integer operation (e.g., add/multiply/etc.) writing to the `x1`-`x31` registers sets the address bits and clears the metadata.
+
+The pure-capability ABIs closely follow the same calling conventions as the base integer and hardware floating-point calling conventions, but since the GPRs are now `YLEN` bits wide the following differences exist:
+
+* Variadic and on-stack arguments use a different register convention (see next subsection).
+* `YLEN` wide scalars are passed in a single argument register if they are of pointer type (including `(u)intptr_t`).
++
+NOTE: For non-pointer scalar types the maximum size passed in a single argument register is still `XLEN` rather than `YLEN`.
+This avoids the implementation difficulty of passing `int64_t` in a single register when `YLEN` is 64 (RV32).
+// It also reflects that the high bits of capability registers cannot be used for computation directly as they need to be copied to another register using `YHIR` first.
+// A future calling convention variant may allow for packing these types in a single register.
+
+* Aggregates up to `2*YLEN` bits are passed in `YLEN` argument register(s) (using the memory layout of the aggregate) if they are at least `YLEN`-bit aligned.
+All less-aligned aggregates follow rules of the underlying base integer or float calling convention (ILP32*/LP64* ABIs).
++
+NOTE: This rule is required to ensure that aggregates that could potentially be used to store capabilities, but do not declare capability members (such as `alignas(16) char bytes[16]`) are passed in capability registers instead of being split into two registers (which would invalidate the capability tag).
+// This does mean that `int64_t` and `struct { int64_t }` have different calling conventions but this behaviour matches the base integer calling convention.
+
+* For aggregates that can be passed in pairs of registers,   they are never split into one register part and one on-stack part.
+  Instead of splitting the entire aggregate is passed on the stack.
+* Aggregates larger than `2*YLEN` or with an alignment larger than the stack alignment are always passed by reference.
+* All other aggregates follow the base calling convention.
+* Unions follow the same rules as aggregates: if they are `YLEN`-bit aligned and less than or equal to `2*YLEN` bits in size,   they are passed in memory layout in `YLEN` registers.
+  Otherwise, the base calling convention rules apply.
+
+Values are returned in the same manner as a first named argument of the same
+type would be passed.
+
+[[pure-cap-on-stack-args]]
+==== Variadic and On-Stack Arguments
+
+In the pure-capability ABIs, variadic and on-stack arguments are handled differently from the base integer calling convention to ensure capability safety and allow for bounded `va_list` implementations.
+
+1. All variadic arguments (those corresponding to the `...` in the function prototype) are passed on the stack.
+They never occupy argument registers `a0`-`a7`.
+Each variadic argument is passed in a `YLEN`-aligned stack slot.
++
+NOTE: Passing all variadic arguments on the stack simplifies the implementation of `va_list` and ensures capability safety.
+Measurements on other architectures (AArch64) have shown that most variadic functions are simply wrappers around a function taking a `va_list`.
+In standard ABIs that pass variadic arguments in registers, the callee must spill these registers to the stack to create a contiguous `va_list` structure, which adds overhead and complicates the implementation.
+Passing all variadic arguments on the stack from the start simplifies these wrappers and avoids complex register-to-stack spilling logic.
+Using `YLEN`-sized slots for all arguments, including those smaller than `YLEN`, further avoids the need for complex logic to determine the offset of each argument.
+This approach has been used successfully in other CHERI-enabled architectures such as Morello and was also adopted by Apple in the variadic calling convention for AArch64 on iOS and macOS.
+
+2. A capability that covers all on-stack arguments on the stack is passed in the `x5` (`t0`) register.
+3. For variadic functions, this capability has its `Store` and `Execute` permissions cleared.
+4. If no on-stack arguments are passed to a variadic function, the `x5` register is set to a `NULL` capability (marked as invalid).
+
+=== IL32PC64E Calling Convention
+
+// TODO: confirm final naming of Y+E base ISA with ARC
+The IL32PC64E calling convention is designed to be usable with the RV32YE base ISA.
+This calling convention is the same as the IL32PC64 calling convention except for the following differences:
+
+* The stack pointer must be aligned to a 128-bit boundary.
++
+NOTE: Maintaining 16-byte alignment even for RV32-based ABIs has benefits for bulk zeroing and capability representability.
+
+* Registers x16-x31 do not participate in the calling convention, so there are only six argument registers, a0-a5, only two callee-saved registers, s0-s1, and only three temporaries, t0-t2.
++
+If used with an ISA that has any of the registers x16-x31 and f0-f31, then these registers are considered temporaries.
+

+L64PC128* and IL32PC64* ABIs::
+The pure-capability RVY ABIs use YLEN bits to represent all pointers and introduce two new base C types to hold capabilities:
+the C standard library on RVY defines `intptr_t`/`uintptr_t` types that can hold capabilities (YLEN values) and integers (XLEN values) alike.
+These types have a YLEN-bit storage size (either 64-bit or 128-bit), however, the maximum arithmetic value that such a type can hold is limited to the maximum _address_ a capability can take (XLEN bits, i.e. YLEN/2).
+Pointers and `intptr_t`/`uintptr_t` must be aligned to YLEN bits.
++
+All other types are otherwise identical to their LP64*/ILP32* counterparts.
++
+NOTE: For very large objects, additional padding and alignment requirements may be introduced to ensure that capabilities referring to the object can be represented precisely.
+The capability compression means the available precision for bounds decreases as the object size increases above a threshold.
+See <<riscv-cheri-spec,the RVY specification>> for details of the restrictions.
+The threshold depends on the ISA but objects smaller than 256 bytes (on RVY32) / 4096 bytes (on RVY64) are never affected.
++
+* **L64PC128, L64PC128F, L64PC128D, and L64PC128Q** use the following type size and
+alignment (based on the L64 convention):
++
+.C/{Cpp} type sizes and alignments for L64PC128
+[cols="4,>2,>3"]
+[width=60%]
+|===
+| Type                   | Size (Bytes)   | Alignment (Bytes)
+| void *                 | 16             | 16
+| `intptr_t`/`uintptr_t` | 16             | 16
+| All other types        | See LP64* ABIs | See LP64* ABIs
+|===
++
+* **IL32PC64, IL32PC64F, IL32PC64D, and IL32PC64E** use the following type size and
+alignment (based on the IL32PC64 convention):
++
+.C/{Cpp} type sizes and alignments for IL32PC64
+[cols="4,>2,>3"]
+[width=60%]
+|===
+| Type                   | Size (Bytes)    | Alignment (Bytes)
+| void *                 | 8               | 8
+| `intptr_t`/`uintptr_t` | 8               | 8
+| All other types        | See ILP32* ABIs | See ILP32* ABIs
+|===
+
 The alignment of `max_align_t` is 16.

+==== va_list, va_start, and va_arg in pure-capability ABIs
+NOTE: In the pure-capability ABIs, the handling of variadic arguments is different.
+All variadic arguments are passed on the stack, and a capability to them is passed in the `x5` (`t0`) register.
+See <<pure-cap-cc>> for details.
+
+As in other ABIs, the `va_list` type is represented as `void *` (which is a capability now).
+The `va_start` macro initializes the `va_list` using the capability provided in `x5`.
+Since all variadic arguments are on the stack, the callee does not need to construct a varargs save area for registers.
+Since the `va_list` now includes bounds information, attempting to use a non-existant argument via `va_arg` will result in a trap.
+
